ArcelorMittal reported a group-wide LTIFR of 0.70 for 2024 (down from 0.92 in 2023, as revised for the new segment structure).

- The 2024 LTIFR of 0.70 is stated in the "Performance in 2024" section of the Health and Safety discussion, alongside a fatality frequency rate of 0.03 and 13 fatalities.
- The Glossary defines LTIFR as Lost Time Injuries ("LTI") per 1,000,000 worked hours, counting both own personnel and contractors.
- A lost time injury is defined in the Glossary as an incident that causes an injury preventing the person from returning to his/her next scheduled shift or work period.

Lerøy's wild-catch volume fell from 75 893 tonnes (HOG) in 2023 to 64 991 tonnes in 2024 — a drop of 10 902 tonnes, or roughly 14%.

- The decline reflects significant quota cuts: cod quotas were reduced by 34% and haddock by 43% year-on-year, with the saithe quota in the northern zone down 6% (WildCatch segment results section).
- The company states that earnings in WildCatch have been significantly affected by the low quota basis and "will remain so for some time," expecting 2025 and probably 2026 to be challenging for the segment (Market and outlook).
- For 2025, the quota decision entails further reductions of 32% for cod and 2% for haddock compared with 2024, while the northern saithe quota is unchanged and the North Sea/southern saithe quota rises 40%; the trawl ladder ("trålstigen") means Havfisk's cod quota falls more than the overall Norwegian decline (Market and outlook).
- The company notes this redistribution of quotas will lead to further job losses in Norway's whitefish industry, and that it continues to focus on improving operational efficiency at sea and onshore to offset lower quotas (Market and outlook).

بودجهٔ سالانهٔ دولت سالانه شش کرور تومان کسری داشت (درآمد پانزده کرور و هزینه بیست‌ویک کرور و نیم تومان)، و کمیسیون دو راه را در نظر گرفت: یکی افزودن به درآمد و دیگری کاستن از هزینه‌ها.

- درآمد دولت در آن هنگام پانزده کرور تومان و نیم و دررفت آن بیست‌ویک کرور تومان و نیم بود که سالانه شش کرور کمی می‌بود و باید با وام پر می‌شد (بخش «کوشش مجلس به برانداختن نوز و پریم»).
- کمیسیون (که وثوق‌الدوله از اعضای آن بود) دو کار را اندیشید: افزودن به درآمد و کاستن از دریافت‌ها (بخش اسفندماه درباره بودجه).
- برای افزونی درآمد سه راه در نظر گرفت: گرفتن «تفاوت عمل» حکمرانان، برانداختن «تیول»، و برانداختن «تسعیر».
- در نهایت کمیسیون مالی از چهار راه سالانه هشت کرور از دررفت‌ها کم کرد: کاستن از مستمری شاهزادگان، جلوگیری از گرفتن مالیات چندبرابر توسط فرمانروایان، برانداختن تیول، و پرداخت جنس به‌جای پول با بهای صد سال پیش (بخش «آمدن محمدعلیمیرزا به مجلس»).

- پیرنیا فوت کوروش را ۵۲۹ ق. م و فتح همدان را ۵۵۰ ق. م می‌داند و بنابراین مدت سلطنت او را از زمان تسخیر همدان ۲۲ سال حساب می‌کند (بخش «مقایسه» و پایان بحث فوت کوروش).

- هرودوت مدت سلطنت کوروش را ۲۸ سال و کتزیاس، دی‌نن و تروگ پومپه سی سال نوشته‌اند، زیرا مورخین مزبور سلطنت سابق او را قبل از تسخیر همدان به حساب آورده‌اند (پایان بحث فوت کوروش).

بند سابله را شیخ سلمان کعبی در جلوی کارون بست تا آب بالا آمده به جوی قبان و جوی‌های دیگر برسد و سراسر زمین‌های آن پیرامون فاریاب و آبادان شود.

- شیخ سلمان مردی آبادی‌دوست بود و برای سرسبزی بخش جنوبی خوزستان در جایی معروف به سابله، نزدیک دهنه جوی قبان، بندی بر کارون بست (بخش «بند بستن شیخ سلمان در جلوی کارون»).
- آبِ بالا آمده به انبوهی به جوی قبان می‌ریخت و از چپ و راست جوی‌های دیگری جدا می‌شد که زمین‌ها را چند فرسنگ در چند فرسنگ فاریاب می‌کرد.
- تاریخ زندیه آن بند را «نمونه سد اسکندر» نامیده است.
- میجر کینیرا نوشت اگر کریم‌خان آن را نشکسته بود، تا قرن‌ها استوار می‌ماند؛ اما مؤلف تذکره بنیاد آن را چوب و نی خاشاک دانسته است.
- کریم‌خان در لشکرکشی بر سر شیخ سلمان، به راهنمایی مردی از عرب، بند سابله را بشکست.
- نتیجه این کار آن شد که قبان روی به ویرانی گذارد و آبادی‌هایش از میان رفت، چنان‌که اکنون در آن سراسر آبادی سرسبزی پیدانتوان کرد؛ و شیخ سلمان نیز پس از آسیب کریم‌خان در پنج سال باقی‌ماندهٔ عمرش دیگر به بستن بند برنگشت و آبادی‌های نتیجهٔ آن بند بار دیگر از میان رفت.

طبق مادهٔ پنجم امتیازنامه، در صورت واگذاری امتیاز به دولت یا شرکت خارجی، امتیاز ملغی می‌شد؛ و در مذاکرات بعدی معلوم شد استاندارد اویل می‌خواست کمپانی نفت جنوب (انگلیسی) را در امتیاز دخیل کند یا با سهم ۱۵۰ یا ۱۴۰ از ۱۰۰۰ (صد پنجاه یا صد چهل در اسهام) شریک سازد.

- مادهٔ ۵ امتیازنامه (مصوب ۳۰ عقرب ۱۳۰۰) تصریح می‌کند کمپانی حق واگذاری امتیاز به دولت یا شرکت خارجی را ندارد و در صورت تخلف، امتیاز ملغی خواهد بود (بند ۵ متن امتیازنامه).
- در مذاکرات بعدی دولت ایران با استاندارد اویل معلوم شد که کمپانی می‌خواهد کمپانی نفت جنوب را در امتیاز دخیل کند یا او را به قرار صد پنجاه یا صد چهل در اسهام خود شرکت دهد (بخش «نفت شمال از میان می‌رود»).
- همین پیشنهاد مشارکت، تحریک احساسات مجلس را برانگیخت و دولت با استناد به مادهٔ پنجم آن را رد کرد.

شهر محمره - روایت لایارد (مأمور انگلیسی کمیسیون مرزی): «نهر موسوم به حفار... جدیدالاحداث است و در ساحل آن نیز شهر محمره را شیخ اعراب کعب بنا نموده است» و «بمرور رودخانهٔ کارون این شهر را بزرگ و وسیع کرده است».
شهر محمره - روایت کسروی: در زمان‌های باستانی آبادی «بیان» در شمال جوی میانه بود که تا قرن چهارم آباد بود و سپس از میان رفت؛ در آخرهای قرن دوازدهم آبادی‌ای به نام «محمره» به جای آن پدید آمد و نخستین بار در تاریخچه کعب در حوادث زمان شیخ غیث با نام «کوت المحمره» آمده که دژی بوده و گروهی از کعبیان در آن نشیمن داشته‌اند؛ سپس میجر کینیرا آن را از دیه‌های خوزستان شمرده و پس از دیری شهری شده که سرپرستش حاجی یوسف پسر حاج مراد او (نیای شیخ خزعل) بود و در زمان شیخ ثامر از اختیار حاج جابر پسر حاج یوسف درآمد و ثامر آن را بندر آزادی ساخت.

مقایسه: لایارد بنا کردن شهر را به شیخ اعراب کعب نسبت می‌دهد و آن را در ساحل نهر حفار (اتصال جدید کارون به شط‌العرب) می‌داند، در حالی که کسروی ریشه شهر را در آبادی باستانی «بیان» می‌داند و می‌گوید محمره در آخرهای قرن دوازدهم به جای آن پدید آمد و نخست دژی کعبی به نام «کوت المحمره» بوده است؛ یعنی هر دو منشأ کعبی برای شهر را تأیید می‌کنند، اما لایارد آن را بنای جدید شیخ کعب در ساحل حفار می‌شمارد و کسروی آن را ادامه و بازآبادانی آبادی کهن‌تر بیان می‌داند.

Hand-wrought silver spoon - Veblen's illustration: some ten to twenty dollars
Machine-made aluminium spoon - Veblen's illustration: some ten to twenty cents

The hand-wrought silver spoon is priced at some ten to twenty dollars, while the machine-made aluminium spoon is valued at no more than some ten to twenty cents — roughly a hundredfold difference, since the silver's material is "some one hundred times more valuable than the baser metal."

The Island - starting point: population of about seven millions, with present produce equal to the support of such a number
The Island - after fifty years (two periods of twenty-five years): population of twenty-eight millions, and the means of subsistence only equal to the support of twenty-one millions

Malthus starts from a population of about seven millions; after fifty years the population would be twenty-eight millions while subsistence would support only twenty-one millions, leaving seven millions unprovided for.

Yes. If a public officer or anyone sees a person attempting to cross a bridge ascertained to be unsafe and there is no time to warn him, they may seize him and turn him back without any real infringement of his liberty (Chapter V, Applications).

- Force is allowed when the danger is certain: the bridge has been ascertained to be unsafe and there is no time to warn him.
- When there is only a danger of mischief, not a certainty, only the person himself can judge the sufficiency of the motive prompting him to incur the risk; then he ought to be only warned of the danger, not forcibly prevented—unless he is a child, delirious, or in some state of excitement or absorption incompatible with the full use of the reflecting faculty.
- Force does not breach liberty because liberty consists in doing what one desires, and the person does not desire to fall into the river.
- Mill also states that the doctrine of liberty applies only to human beings in the maturity of their faculties: it does not apply to children or young persons below the legal age, who must be protected against their own actions, nor to backward states of society still in their nonage, where despotism may be legitimate if it effects their improvement (Chapter I, Introductory).

American back settlements - late 18th century: they doubled their number in fifteen years.

Comparison: 300–400 years divided by 15 years gives roughly 20 to 27 times faster, so the American back settlements doubled their population roughly twenty to twenty-five times faster than the principal states of modern Europe.

Veblen concedes that the corset impairs the personal attractions of the wearer, but this loss is offset by the gain in reputability that comes from her visibly increased expensiveness and infirmity (evidence [1], Chapter Seven, "Dress as an Expression of the Pecuniary Culture"). The corset has fallen into disuse among the wealthiest class because that class has grown large enough that any aspersion on the score of enforced manual employment would be idle and harmless calumny, so the pretense of leisure is no longer needed. It persists among the later accessions to wealth in advanced industrial communities, who have not yet divested themselves of the plebeian canons of taste carried over from their lower pecuniary grade, and among the wealthy classes of countries with a lower, more archaic industrial structure. Veblen says the corset thus continues wherever it serves its purpose as evidence of honorific leisure by arguing physical disability in the wearer, persisting through the period of "snobbery"—the transition from a lower to an upper level of pecuniary culture.

On the Origin of Species (1st edition, 1859): assumes the elephant breeds when thirty years old and goes on breeding till ninety years old, bringing forth three pair of young in this interval; result: at the end of the fifth century there would be alive fifteen million elephants, descended from the first pair.

On the Origin of Species (6th edition, 1872): assumes it is safest to assume the elephant begins breeding when thirty years old, goes on breeding till ninety years old, bringing forth six young in the interval, and surviving till one hundred years old; result: after a period of from 740 to 750 years there would be nearly nineteen million elephants alive descended from the first pair.

Between editions, Darwin changed the assumption from three pair of young (six offspring) to six young, added the assumption of surviving till one hundred years old, and changed the result from fifteen million elephants at the end of the fifth century to nearly nineteen million elephants after 740 to 750 years.

Darwin says the struggle for existence is "the doctrine of Malthus applied with manifold force to the whole animal and vegetable kingdoms" (Chapter III, Struggle for Existence, both editions).

According to Malthus's own Essay on the Principle of Population (1798):

- Population, when unchecked, increases in a geometrical ratio, while subsistence increases only in an arithmetical ratio (Chapter 1).
- He illustrates this with the series 1, 2, 4, 8, 16... for population versus 1, 2, 3, 4, 5... for subsistence (Chapter 2).
- Taking the United States as his example, where checks to early marriage were fewest, he adopts as his rule that unchecked population doubles every twenty-five years (Chapter 2).

Mill - On Liberty: The most dangerous reach is social tyranny exercised through prevailing opinion and feeling—society imposing its own ideas and practices as rules of conduct on dissenters, penetrating deeply into the details of life and "enslaving the soul itself," fettering individuality without legal penalties.

Tocqueville - Democracy in America: The most dangerous reach is the majority's moral power over opinion and the mind—once the majority decides, all discussion ceases; democratic republics leave the body free but enslave the soul, depriving dissenters of esteem, career, and companionship rather than using physical force.

Comparison: Both warn that the majority's gravest tyranny operates not through laws or officials but over thought and opinion—Mill calls it the tyranny of the prevailing opinion that crushes individuality, while Tocqueville describes a despotism that "sways the minds of men," leaving bodies free but souls enslaved.

Malthus - 1798 Essay: population, when unchecked, doubles every twenty-five years (geometrical ratio)
Tocqueville - 1790: population nearly 4,000,000 (census figure 3,929,328)
Tocqueville - 1830: population nearly 13,000,000 (census figure 12,856,165)
Tocqueville - doubling period: the number of inhabitants has about doubled every twenty-two years since the first settlement of the British colonies

The figures bear Malthus out roughly: from about 4,000,000 to about 13,000,000 in forty years is slightly more than a tripling, implying a doubling period of about twenty-five years (4→8→13 in two doublings over 40 years). Tocqueville himself gives a doubling period of twenty-two years, slightly faster than Malthus's rule.

Mill - On Liberty, Ch. IV: In the United States, "the feeling of the majority, to whom any appearance of a more showy or costly style of living than they can hope to rival is disagreeable, operates as a tolerably effectual sumptuary law," so that "in many parts of the Union it is really difficult for a person possessing a very large income, to find any mode of spending it, which will not incur popular disapprobation."

Veblen - The Theory of the Leisure Class: The motive behind such showy spending is pecuniary emulation and conspicuous consumption—the desire to excel others in wealth, since "the possession of wealth confers honour; it is an invidious distinction," and costly display of goods is "a means of reputability to the gentleman of leisure."

Comparison: Mill describes majority feeling as a social restraint (an informal "sumptuary law") that blocks the showy expenditure of large incomes; Veblen's theory explains that the spending being restrained is motivated by emulation—the wish to display wealth and rank above one's neighbours—so the majority's disapproval is itself an invidious reaction against others' attempts at pecuniary superiority.

مبانی این پاسخ:
1. طبق ماده 946 قانون مدنی، زوج از تمام اموال زوجه ارث می‌برد و زوجه در صورت فرزنددار بودن زوج، یک‌هشتم از عین اموال منقول و یک‌هشتم از قیمت اموال غیرمنقول اعم از عرصه و اعیان ارث می‌برد.
2. در این فرض چون زوج فرزند (پسر) دارد، سهم زوجه یک‌هشتم است؛ اگر فرزندی نداشت، سهم او یک‌چهارم می‌شد (ماده 946).
3. خودرو اموال منقول است، بنابراین زوجه یک‌هشتم عین آن را می‌برد؛ اما آپارتمان غیرمنقول است و سهم زوجه یک‌هشتم از قیمت آن خواهد بود (ماده 946).
4. طبق ماده 948، هرگاه ورثه از ادای قیمت امتناع کنند، زن می‌تواند حق خود را از عین اموال استیفا کند.

طبق اصل ۹۶، تشخیص عدم مغایرت مصوبات مجلس با احکام اسلام با اکثریت فقهای شورای نگهبان است، یعنی از ۶ فقیه دست‌کم ۴ رأی لازم است. تشخیص عدم تعارض با قانون اساسی بر عهده اکثریت همه اعضای شورا (۱۲ نفر) است، یعنی دست‌کم ۷ رأی لازم است.

قانون تجارت فعلی - ماده ۱۱: دفاتر مذکور در ماده ۶ به استثنای دفتر کپیه قبل از آن که در آن چیزی نوشته شده باشد به توسط نماینده اداره ثبت (که مطابق نظام‌نامه وزارت عدلیه معین می‌شود) امضا می‌شود؛ دفتر کپیه از امضاء معاف است ولی اوراق آن باید نمره ترتیبی داشته باشد.

مقایسه: در هر دو قانون دفتر کپیه از امضاء معاف است و سایر دفاتر باید پیش از نوشتن امضا شوند؛ تفاوت در مقام امضاکننده است: در قانون ۱۳۰۳ رئیس محکمه تجارت یا قضات عدلیه یا صاحب‌منصبان پارکه یا حاکم محل، و در قانون فعلی نماینده اداره ثبت (مطابق نظام‌نامه وزارت عدلیه) امضا می‌کند.

در قانون ۱۳۴۵ بالاترین نرخ ۵۵ درصد بود که اصلاحیهٔ ۱۳۵۱ آن را به ۶۰ درصد افزایش داد؛ نرخ‌های جدید از درآمدهای تحصیلی اول سال ۱۳۵۲ به بعد (و سال مالی اشخاص حقوقی که در ۱۳۵۲ به بعد خاتمه می‌یابد) اعمال می‌شد.

قانون مالیات‌های مستقیم 1345 - تبصره 9 ماده 20: هر کس ملک شخصی محل سکونت خود را به دیگری به اجاره واگذار کند و خود خانه دیگری برای سکونت خویش اجاره کند، در احتساب درآمد مشمول مالیات مستغلات او میزان مال‌الاجاره‌ای که به موجب سند رسمی می‌پردازد از کل مال‌الاجاره‌های دریافتی او کسر خواهد شد.
قانون اصلاح 1351 - بند 5 ج: عبارت «ملک شخصی محل سکونت خود را» به عبارت «خانه خود را» اصلاح و بعد از عبارت «به موجب سند رسمی» عبارت «یا قرارداد عادی» اضافه می‌شود.

طبق قانون 1345، کسر مال‌الاجاره پرداختی فقط در صورتی ممکن بود که پرداخت به موجب سند رسمی باشد. اصلاحیه 1351 دامنه حکم را گسترش داد: شرط «ملک شخصی محل سکونت» به «خانه» تغییر یافت و اجاره با «قرارداد عادی» نیز در کنار سند رسمی پذیرفته شد.

No — both fail under the GDPR.

- Recital 32 states that silence, pre-ticked boxes or inactivity should not constitute consent; consent must be a clear affirmative act, so the pre-ticked box is not valid consent.
- Article 4(1)(11) defines consent as a freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous indication by a statement or clear affirmative action, which a pre-ticked box does not meet.
- Article 7(3) requires that it shall be as easy to withdraw consent as to give it, so requiring a signed letter by post is not acceptable.
- Article 7(3) also provides that withdrawal must not affect the lawfulness of processing based on consent before its withdrawal, and the data subject must be informed of the right to withdraw before giving consent.
- Recital 43 adds that consent is presumed not freely given if performance of a contract, including provision of a service, is made dependent on consent that is not necessary for that performance.

Yes — the retailer's use is caught by the prohibition; the lab's use is not.

- Article 5(1)(f) prohibits placing on the market, putting into service, or using AI systems to infer emotions of natural persons in the areas of workplace and education institutions, except where the use is intended for medical or safety reasons.
- The retailer's use to monitor staff mood in its shops is emotion inference in the workplace, and no medical or safety exception applies, so it falls under the prohibition.
- The university lab's use is not caught because Article 2(6) excludes from the Regulation's scope AI systems specifically developed and put into service for the sole purpose of scientific research and development.
- Note that the exclusion applies only to the research use: once the same system is placed on the market and put into service by the retailer for workplace mood monitoring, the prohibition in Article 5(1)(f) applies to that use.

The platform must give the user a clear and specific statement of reasons, and the user can challenge the removal through an internal complaint-handling system that is electronic and free of charge, available for at least six months starting from the day the user is informed of the decision.

- Statement of reasons (Article 17(1)(a), (3)): for restrictions such as removal of content, the provider of hosting services must give a clear and specific statement of reasons containing, among other things, the type of restriction and its territorial scope and duration, the facts and circumstances relied on, whether automated means were used, the legal or contractual ground, and clear information on redress possibilities.
- Complaint system (Article 20(1)): providers of online platforms must give recipients of the service, including those who submitted a notice, access to an effective internal complaint-handling system to lodge complaints electronically and free of charge against decisions to remove or disable access to information.
- Duration and starting point (Article 20(2)): the period of at least six months starts on the day the recipient of the service is informed about the decision in accordance with Article 16(5) or Article 17.

No — the short-term right to reject is lost. Under section 22(3), the time limit is the end of 30 days beginning with the first day after ownership/possession has been transferred and the goods have been delivered, so ten weeks is too late (section 22(1)).

The next remedy is the right to repair or replacement under section 23: the trader must repair or replace within a reasonable time and without significant inconvenience, bearing the costs (section 23(2)). If that fails or is impossible/disproportionate, the consumer then has the right to a price reduction or the final right to reject (sections 19(3)(c) and 24(5)).

On the burden of proof: no, the consumer does not have to prove the fault existed at delivery. Section 19(14) provides that goods which do not conform at any time within six months of delivery must be taken not to have conformed on the day of delivery, unless it is established that they did conform on that day or the presumption is incompatible with the nature of the goods or the failure (section 19(15)).

Digital Services Act - Article 33(1): online platforms and online search engines with a number of average monthly active recipients of the service in the Union equal to or higher than 45 million, designated as very large online platforms or very large online search engines.

Digital Markets Act - Article 3(2)(b): a core platform service that in the last financial year has at least 45 million monthly active end users established or located in the Union and at least 10 000 yearly active business users established in the Union, identified and calculated in accordance with the methodology and indicators set out in the Annex.

The DSA counts average monthly active recipients of the service in the Union (≥45 million) for designating very large online platforms/search engines, while the DMA counts monthly active end users established or located in the Union (≥45 million) and additionally requires at least 10 000 yearly active business users established in the Union, with the thresholds needing to be met in each of the last three financial years for the presumption of an entrenched and durable position.

AI Act (prohibited AI practice, Art. 99(3)): 7 % of total worldwide annual turnover
Digital Services Act (VLOP/VLOSE non-compliance, Art. 74(1)): 6 % of total worldwide annual turnover
Digital Markets Act (first non-compliance, Art. 30(1)): 10 % of total worldwide turnover

Ranked from highest to lowest, the DMA fine (10 %) exceeds the AI Act fine (7 %), which in turn exceeds the DSA fine (6 %).

The AI Act uses the definition of 'personal data' from the GDPR. Article 3(50) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 defines 'personal data' as "personal data as defined in Article 4, point (1), of Regulation (EU) 2016/679". That GDPR definition, in Article 4(1), states that 'personal data' means any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person ('data subject'), where an identifiable natural person is one who can be identified, directly or indirectly, in particular by reference to an identifier such as a name, an identification number, location data, an online identifier or to one or more factors specific to the physical, physiological, genetic, mental, economic, cultural or social identity of that natural person.

UK police force - Data Protection Act 2018, Part 3 breach of section 35: higher maximum amount, which for a non-undertaking is £17,500,000 (section 157(2)(a) and (5)(b)).
EU company - GDPR breach of basic principles for processing (Articles 5, 6, 7 and 9): up to 20 000 000 EUR, or in the case of an undertaking, up to 4 % of the total worldwide annual turnover of the preceding financial year, whichever is higher (Article 83(5)(a)).

The UK police force faces a fixed maximum of £17,500,000, while the EU company faces up to 20 000 000 EUR or 4 % of its annual worldwide turnover, whichever is higher — so the EU maximum is turnover-based and could exceed the UK figure.

AI Act (general case, serious incident reporting) - Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Article 73(2): not later than 15 days after the provider or, where applicable, the deployer becomes aware of the serious incident
GDPR (personal data breach notification) - Regulation (EU) 2016/679, Article 33(1): without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than 72 hours after having become aware of it

The GDPR deadline (72 hours) is shorter than the AI Act general deadline (15 days).
